topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the opening framing, course structure, and learning outcomes for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Differentiation and Tissue Architecture
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer develops as a failure of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture driven by genetic and epigenetic alterations, and how this biology is investigated.

topics.label: Mechanisms and Histology of Invasion and Metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate the mechanisms of tumor invasion and metastasis, highlighting the adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence as a histological model of progression.

topics.label: Behavior and Nomenclature of Benign and Malignant Tumors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical behavior, risks, and standardized naming conventions that distinguish benign from malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Pathophysiological Mechanisms of Cancer Morbidity and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the physical, metabolic, and metastatic mechanisms through which tumors cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Epidemiology and Comparative Oncology Across Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey the distribution, frequency, and evolutionary occurrence of cancer across human populations and other animal species.

topics.label: Principles and Modalities of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the rationale, implementation, and varying efficacy of population-level cancer screening strategies.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This topic provides the closing framing, summarizing the session and pointing toward upcoming practicals and lectures.
